Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. statement: Fix an integer n ≥ 1 and, at a fixed mesh, a finite physical-layer setup as above. All layer counts and all inserted edge matrices are fixed before even N → ∞. Let Bout,N and Bin,N be products of the corresponding ξ- and ζ-twist rows in (8.43), each containing at least n rows. Every row is at a physical angle ±γ0. For x, y ∈ {−γ0, γ0}, define either Dlow N = Eout,N c NN (x)Ein,N , (8.44) Dhigh N = Ex out,N c NN (x)Ex in,N − eiτ(x−y) Ey out,N c NN (y)Ey in,N . (8.45) Each E is a separately even product of at most a fixed L physical rows with the corresponding twist. The lists for the two high terms may differ, but the exterior networks in (8.41) are common to them. Every row in these displays has its own divisor ΛN . Set, for a = low, high, Ca N = 1 |SN | X σ∈SN ⟨ψout,σ,N , Bout,N Da N Bin,N ψin,σ,N ⟩GN . (8.46) 132 Then Ca = limN→∞, N even Ca N and Rin, Rout, the corresponding limits of (8.41), exist. They are the square-plane scalar coefficient and its finite nonnegative reflected vacuum ratios. They satisfy |Clow | ≤ Cλ,Ln−1+ρ p RoutRin, (8.47) |Chigh | ≤ Cλ,Ln−1−ρ p RoutRin. (8.48) The analogous fixed-diagram reflection across an ordinary tile-axis cut gives the plane Cauchy– Schwarz inequality with its two reflected ratios.
